	The Accountant is responsible for the day-to-day financial and accounting operations of the Maiduguri Branch, ensuring accurate bookkeeping, timely reporting, and strict compliance with company policy and statutory requirements.

	Prepare periodic (daily, weekly, monthly) branch financial reports for submission to Head Office.
	Prepare monthly management accounts, including income statements, balance sheet items, and variance analysis for the branch.
	Support the preparation of the branch&#39;s annual budget and monitor actual performance against it.

	Process supplier invoices and staff expense claims for the branch, ensuring accuracy and appropriate approval.
	Monitor and follow up on outstanding receivables/debtors for the branch.
	Support periodic stocktakes and reconcile branch inventory records with financial accounts, where applicable.


Compliance &amp; Internal Controls:


	Ensure branch financial operations comply with company policies, accounting standards, and relevant statutory/tax regulations.
	Support internal and external audit exercises by providing accurate records and responding to audit queries.
	Identify and escalate control weaknesses or compliance risks at branch level.


Payroll &amp; Statutory Remittances:


	Support branch-level payroll input and verification, working with Head Office HR/Finance as required.
	Assist with the computation and timely remittance of statutory deductions (e.g. PAYE, pension) for branch staff, where applicable.


Stakeholder Liaison:


	Serve as the primary point of contact for finance-related matters at the branch, liaising with the Branch Manager, Head Office Finance team, vendors, and customers.
	Respond to finance queries from branch staff and customers in a professional and timely manner.

Education:


	Bachelor&#39;s Degree (HND or BSc) in Accounting, Finance, Economics, or a related field.
	Professional accounting qualification (e.g. ICAN, ACCA) obtained or in progress is an advantage.


Experience:


	Minimum of 2&ndash;4 years of relevant accounting/bookkeeping experience, ideally in a branch or retail finance environment.
	Experience managing petty cash, bank reconciliations, and day-to-day transaction processing.
	Prior exposure to statutory compliance and tax remittance processes in Nigeria is an advantage.
	Experience working with minimal on-site supervision and reporting into a Head Office function.


Knowledge &amp; Technical Skills:


	Sound knowledge of bookkeeping principles and basic accounting standards.
	Proficient in Microsoft Excel; working knowledge of accounting software (e.g. Sage, QuickBooks, or company ERP) preferred.
	Good understanding of cash handling controls and reconciliation procedures.
	Basic knowledge of Nigerian tax and statutory remittance requirements (PAYE, pension, etc.).


Core Competencies:


	Accuracy and attention to detail &mdash; maintains precise, error-free financial records.
	Integrity &mdash; trusted to handle cash and sensitive financial information responsibly.
	Organisation and time management &mdash; meets reporting deadlines consistently.
	Communication &mdash; liaises effectively with branch staff, Head Office, and external parties.
	Problem-solving &mdash; identifies and resolves discrepancies proactively.
	Adaptability &mdash; comfortable working independently in a branch setting with periodic Head Office oversight.


Other Requirements:


	Must be a resident of, or willing to relocate to, Maiduguri.
	Willingness to travel to Head Office or other branches for training/reporting as required.
	High level of discretion and confidentiality when handling financial data.

N500,000 - N1,000,000 per month.

Accountant Job at Le Treda Consult




        
    

        
        Le Treda Consult - Our client is a conglomerate with operations across Nigeria’s most dynamic economic sectors. The Group holds leadership positions in all five companies, all sharing a simple yet effective corporate vision: providing customers with unparalleled satisfaction.

The Group operates in several sectors critical to Nigeria’s sustained development: agriculture, alternative energy, backup power supply systems, networking and data transmission, ICT infrastructure development, and commercial vehicle sales and servicing. We operate a network of ten branches, ensuring the availability of our products and services throughout Nigeria, with our reach extending to the remotest corners of the country.

They are recruiting to fill the position below:
     

            
    



 Job Position: Accountant

Job Locations: Adamawa, Gombe, Yobe, and Maiduguri - Borno
Employment Type: Full-time

Position Summary


	The Accountant is responsible for the day-to-day financial and accounting operations of the Maiduguri Branch, ensuring accurate bookkeeping, timely reporting, and strict compliance with company policy and statutory requirements.
	The role safeguards branch cash and assets, supports budgeting and cost control, and acts as the key financial liaison between the branch and Head Office, ensuring the branch's accounts are audit-ready at all times.


Key Responsibilities
Bookkeeping & Financial Records:


	Maintain accurate and up-to-date books of account for the branch, including ledgers, journals, and supporting schedules.
	Post and reconcile daily financial transactions, including sales, purchases, receipts, and payments.
	Ensure all financial transactions are properly authorised, documented, and filed in line with company policy.


Cash & Bank Management:


	Manage branch petty cash, ensuring proper authorisation, documentation, and replenishment.
	Prepare and perform daily/weekly bank reconciliations for all branch accounts.
	Monitor branch cash flow and escalate shortfalls or irregularities promptly.
	Ensure cash and cheques are banked promptly and securely in line with company procedure.


Reporting:


	Prepare periodic (daily, weekly, monthly) branch financial reports for submission to Head Office.
	Prepare monthly management accounts, including income statements, balance sheet items, and variance analysis for the branch.
	Support the preparation of the branch's annual budget and monitor actual performance against it.


Payables, Receivables & Inventory:


	Process supplier invoices and staff expense claims for the branch, ensuring accuracy and appropriate approval.
	Monitor and follow up on outstanding receivables/debtors for the branch.
	Support periodic stocktakes and reconcile branch inventory records with financial accounts, where applicable.


Compliance & Internal Controls:


	Ensure branch financial operations comply with company policies, accounting standards, and relevant statutory/tax regulations.
	Support internal and external audit exercises by providing accurate records and responding to audit queries.
	Identify and escalate control weaknesses or compliance risks at branch level.


Payroll & Statutory Remittances:


	Support branch-level payroll input and verification, working with Head Office HR/Finance as required.
	Assist with the computation and timely remittance of statutory deductions (e.g. PAYE, pension) for branch staff, where applicable.


Stakeholder Liaison:


	Serve as the primary point of contact for finance-related matters at the branch, liaising with the Branch Manager, Head Office Finance team, vendors, and customers.
	Respond to finance queries from branch staff and customers in a professional and timely manner.


Person Specification
Education:


	Bachelor's Degree (HND or BSc) in Accounting, Finance, Economics, or a related field.
	Professional accounting qualification (e.g. ICAN, ACCA) obtained or in progress is an advantage.


Experience:


	Minimum of 2–4 years of relevant accounting/bookkeeping experience, ideally in a branch or retail finance environment.
	Experience managing petty cash, bank reconciliations, and day-to-day transaction processing.
	Prior exposure to statutory compliance and tax remittance processes in Nigeria is an advantage.
	Experience working with minimal on-site supervision and reporting into a Head Office function.


Knowledge & Technical Skills:


	Sound knowledge of bookkeeping principles and basic accounting standards.
	Proficient in Microsoft Excel; working knowledge of accounting software (e.g. Sage, QuickBooks, or company ERP) preferred.
	Good understanding of cash handling controls and reconciliation procedures.
	Basic knowledge of Nigerian tax and statutory remittance requirements (PAYE, pension, etc.).


Core Competencies:


	Accuracy and attention to detail — maintains precise, error-free financial records.
	Integrity — trusted to handle cash and sensitive financial information responsibly.
	Organisation and time management — meets reporting deadlines consistently.
	Communication — liaises effectively with branch staff, Head Office, and external parties.
	Problem-solving — identifies and resolves discrepancies proactively.
	Adaptability — comfortable working independently in a branch setting with periodic Head Office oversight.


Other Requirements:


	Must be a resident of, or willing to relocate to, Maiduguri.
	Willingness to travel to Head Office or other branches for training/reporting as required.

N500,000 - N1,000,000 per month.

Sales Executive Job at Skynet Worldwide Express




        
    

        
        Skynet Worldwide Express - An International Courier & Cargo Logistics company with offices in major cities in the world is recruiting to fill the position below:

We are recruiting to fill the position below:

 Job Position: Sales Executive

Job Location: Abuja

Key Responsibilities
The successful candidate will be responsible for:
     

            
    




	Supervising and coordinating the sales team to achieve set targets.
	Developing and implementing effective sales strategies to drive revenue growth.
	Identifying and pursuing new business opportunities within the courier and logistics market.
	Managing and maintaining strong relationships with existing and prospective clients.
	Monitoring individual and team sales performance and providing regular reports to management.
	Setting sales targets and ensuring the team consistently meets or exceeds expectations.
	Conducting market research to identify new opportunities, customer needs, and industry trends.
	Following up on leads, prospects, quotations, and business opportunities.
	Supporting the team in developing and maintaining a strong customer base.
	Ensuring excellent customer service and prompt resolution of client concerns.
	Coaching, motivating, and providing guidance to sales team members.
	Collaborating with Operations and other departments to ensure seamless service delivery.


Requirements


	Minimum of 3 years of experience in Sales, Business Development, or a related role, preferably within the courier, logistics, transportation, or service industry.
	Proven experience in sales supervision or team leadership.
	Strong knowledge of sales processes, business development, and customer relationship management.
	Demonstrated ability to achieve and exceed sales targets.
	Excellent communication, negotiation, persuasion, and interpersonal skills.
	Strong leadership, analytical, and problem-solving abilities.
	Ability to work independently and effectively manage multiple priorities.
	Must be target-driven, proactive, organized, and results-oriented.
	Good knowledge of the Abuja market and surrounding business environment will be an added advantage.


Method of Application
Interested and qualified candidates should send their updated CV to: [email protected] using the Job Position as the subject of the mail.

Note: Only shortlisted candidates who meet the requirements will be contacted.
